short: Four times prime minister, and the Liberal conscience of Victorian Britain.
full:
William Gladstone formed four governments between 1868 and 1894, entering the Commons as a Tory and leaving as the standard-bearer of Liberalism. His first ministry disestablished the Irish church, opened the civil service to competitive examination, abolished the purchase of army commissions, introduced the secret ballot and made elementary education available across England and Wales. His budgets as chancellor had already stripped away hundreds of tariffs.

Ireland consumed his later career. Convinced the Union could survive only with self-government, he introduced Home Rule bills in 1886 and 1893; the first split the Liberal Party and brought down his government within months, the second passed the Commons and was killed by the Lords. He also extended the county franchise in 1884, adding some six million voters over two reform acts. He resigned in March 1894, aged eighty-four. Victoria disliked him intensely and never troubled to disguise it.
